description:
FILED s473w (Opus, 2026-09-09) from the #1502 CPAN-board census.

Class::Method::Modifiers installs `before`/`after`/`around` wrappers by
replacing a sub in a class's stash.  Three of its board files die outright and
one gets the ORDER wrong; perl passes all four.

  002-cache.t   FAIL 0/0 (perl 3/0)   dies:
                "FINALIZE-INHERITANCE was called on a forward referenced class"
  003-basic.t   FAIL 0/0 (perl 6/0)   same death
  081-sub-and-modifier.t FAIL 0/0 (perl 28/0)  dies:
                "The method 'orig' is not found in the inheritance hierarchy
                 for class MyParent2"
  100-class-mop-method-modifiers.t  PARTIAL 1/2 (perl 3/0): the collected
                results ARRAY differs from perl's â a modifier ordering
                divergence, not a death.

REPRODUCE:
    tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Class-Method-Modifiers-2.15-0 t/002-cache.t

WHAT THE TWO DEATHS SAY.  Both are CLOS-level, i.e. PCL's OO model, not the
module's perl:
  * "forward referenced class" is SBCL telling us `finalize-inheritance` ran on
    a class created by `p-defclass` with a parent that has only been NAMED, not
    defined.  A modifier is installed into a class whose parent's `p-defclass`
    has not been read yet â the same READ-TIME ordering family as #1570, one
    level up (there the reader dies; here the class system does).
  * "'orig' is not found in the inheritance hierarchy" is the `around`
    wrapper's own inner sub being looked up as a METHOD on the parent class.

WHERE TO START: `p-defclass` / the MRO re-declaration in Pl/Parser2.pm (the
same emission #1570 names), plus `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`'s method-installation
path.  A single probe file that does `around` on a class whose parent is
declared LATER in the file should reproduce the first death in a dozen lines â
write that before touching anything.

BOARD COST: 3 files with zero rows (perl 3 + 6 + 28 = 37 rows behind them) and
2 failing rows in a fourth.
